methodologyNotes: This dataset covers 13 current-generation FDM and MSLA resin 3D printers spanning entry-level to prosumer segments, including models from Bambu Lab, Prusa, Creality, Anycubic, Elegoo, and Sovol. Specifications were re-verified against manufacturer product pages (bambulab.com, prusa3d.com, store.creality.com, store.anycubic.com, us.elegoo.com, sovol3d.com), official spec sheets, and corroborated by reputable review/retail sources (Tom's Hardware, 3D Printing Industry, MatterHackers, West3D, 3DPros database). priceUsd reflects published US MSRP from the manufacturer's US storefront or an official US reseller; where a product is frequently discounted, the regular published price is used and the priceNote records typical street/sale pricing. Boolean specKeys (auto_leveling, multicolor, enclosed) are true only when the feature is present on the base unit without additional purchase (so single-color FDM bases whose multicolor requires a separately purchased AMS/ACE unit are multicolor=false; the H2D is multicolor=true because its dual hardened-steel nozzles do 2-material printing natively). Resin (MSLA) printers leave max_speed_mms and max_hotend_temp_c null as inapplicable. accessedAt 2026-06-15.

The Elegoo US store product page confirms the CoreXY FDM printer (listed under "FDM 3D Printers"), Build Volume 256 × 256 × 256 mm, up to 500 mm/s Velocity (20,000 mm/s² Acceleration), a 320 °C brass-hardened steel nozzle, a fully enclosed chamber with tempered glass door, and Full-Auto Calibration (auto bed leveling); it lists the regular price $419.99 with a current summer-sale price of $309.00 (-26%). The Amazon "ELEGOO Official US" listing corroborates via its specification table: Max Printing Speed 500 mm/s, Build Volume 256 × 256 × 256 mm (W × D × H), Max Hot End Temp. 320 °C, Shell Enclosed (Metal & Glass), Leveling Method Auto-Leveling; and shows "Date First Available June 19, 2025," supporting release_year 2025. Multicolor is not native to the base unit (CANVAS multicolor is a separate SKU; a customer review states "it doesnt do multiple colors"), so multicolor=false. Exact model confirmed: Amazon "Item model number Centauri Carbon" (ASIN B0FDQP54X8), not a sibling/variant. All 8 spec keys, priceUsd, and releaseDate verified.

products.name: Creality K1C
products.priceNote: MatterHackers List Price $399.00 (regular published US reseller price); currently on sale $359.00 (Save $30, offer ends 6/30). The manufacturer Creality product page shows no price.
products.provenance: The official Creality K1C product page confirmed FDM (fused deposition modeling), a 220*220*250mm build volume, ≤600mm/s max printing speed, ≤300℃ nozzle temperature, hands-free auto leveling, and an enclosed design (glass door with acrylic sides and lid forming a thermal enclosure). MatterHackers corroborated each verbatim in its spec table (Technology Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM), Build Volume 220mm × 220mm × 250mm, Max Hotend Temperature 300°C, Max Speed of Toolhead 600mm/s, Enclosed Yes/✓, Automatic Bed Leveling ✓) and supplied the US price: List Price $399.00 with a current sale at $359.00 (Save $30, offer ends 6/30). Multicolor is false on the base unit: the Creality page presents the CFS as a separately purchased upgrade accessory kit for multicolor printing and MatterHackers lists Extrusion: Single, matching the dataset methodology (multicolor true only when native to the base unit). Release year/date was NULLED on re-verification: neither the source (Creality) nor the corroboration (MatterHackers) page states a release year — the prior "2024" value came from 3DPros, which is not a re-fetched source/corroboration URL and cannot be confirmed verbatim.

products.name: Prusa XL
products.priceNote: US retailer Printed Solid (official US Prusa distributor) lists the base single-toolhead unit verbatim as "Semi Assembled 1 Toolhead $2,190"; same page shows "Semi Assembled 2 Toolhead $2,790" and "Semi Assembled 5 Toolhead $3,390". priceUsd reflects the $2,190 single-toolhead base. (Prusa's own EU store shows the single-toolhead at €2,299 / $2,418.79 incl. VAT — not used as it bundles EU VAT.)
products.provenance: Re-fetched both URLs via fetch-clean.mjs and verified every non-null field verbatim. Exact model confirmed as the single-toolhead Prusa XL on BOTH pages (Prusa3D: "Original Prusa XL Single-toolhead 3D Printer"; Printed Solid: "Semi Assembled 1 Toolhead $2,190") — no variant/capacity mismatch. Verified: Build Volume "360×360×360 mm" (both pages); Max Nozzle Temperature "290 °C / 554 °F" (both); bed calibration "Automatic, Mesh Bed Leveling" / "Fully automatic Mesh Bed Leveling via Loadcell sensor" → auto_leveling=true; "Chamber: No (optional Enclosure as a separate add-on)" / "Enclosure / Chamber: Optional add-on" → enclosed=false; US price "$2,190.00" and "Semi Assembled 1 Toolhead $2,190" (Printed Solid). technology="FDM" supported — the corroboration page explicitly calls it an "FFF printer" (TechRadar) and the machine is unambiguously fused-filament (1.75 mm filament, Nextruder direct-drive extruder, nozzle, heatbed); FDM is the standard synonym for FFF. multicolor=false because the priced base is the single-toolhead unit, which both pages state requires separately purchased toolhead upgrades ("Start with a single-tool machine and then expand it to 2 or 5 toolheads") — consistent with dataset methodology. max_speed_mms=null (neither page publishes a mm/s speed rating). release_year=null and releaseDate=null (neither page states an explicit numeric release year; "the 2025 iteration" describes the current version, not the original release). All 6 non-null specs plus priceUsd verified against fetched text; nothing required nulling.

Max 600mm/s ... 250 * 250 * 250mm", shown under Anycubic's "FDM 3D Printer" line, "Fully Enclosed: Yes") corroborates the 600 mm/s speed, build volume, 320℃ hotend, FDM/CoreXY construction and LeviQ3.0 leveling. priceUsd $349 is the base Kobra S1 price published on the Anycubic US storefront (shown as a sale from a $549 compare-at "regular price", Save $200); the Kobra S1 Combo bundle is $399. releaseDate and release_year were nulled: neither the source nor the corroboration page states a January 2025 (or any) launch month — the Anycubic store page lists no launch date, and Amazon shows "Date First Available July 27, 2024," which contradicts a 2025-01 date.
